transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, things at work have been getting confusing. I manage a retail store, and lately, when I try to explain the inventory numbers or go over the weekend schedule with my team, my words just... they get all jumbled up. 

I'll start talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm talking about Thursdays, and then the grill at my church, and then how my boss sounded on the phone. It makes sense in my head at first, but then I look at my employees, and they're just staring at me. They can't follow what I'm saying at all. It's happening a lot, and it's making it really hard to do my job.
When you're speaking, do you feel like your thoughts are jumping around, even though they make sense to you at the time?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, it feels completely normal in my head while it's happening. I feel like there's a clear reason why I go from the inventory trucks, to Thursday, to the church grill, and then to how my boss sounded. To me, they're all connected. 

But when the words actually come out of my mouth, they just jump from topic to topic. I really only know it's a problem because of those blank stares I get from my team when they can't follow me.
Have you ever experienced things that others around you don't seem to experience—like hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or having unusual beliefs that other people don't share?

No, I can't say that I have. I don't hear any voices or see anything that isn't really there. And as for unusual beliefs... no, I don't think so. It's really just the trouble with my words getting tangled up when I'm trying to talk to my team at the store. That's the only thing that's been bothering me.

Do you ever feel like your thoughts are disconnected or don't make sense to you, even when you're not trying to talk to someone else? Like your mind jumps around even when you're just thinking to yourself?

No, I don't think so. When I'm just... thinking to myself, everything feels fine. My thoughts make perfect sense to me in my own head. I can plan out the whole week for the store or figure out the inventory without any problem. It really only gets confusing when I try to actually say it out loud to somebody else.
Have you ever had thoughts that felt like they were being inserted into your mind, or that your thoughts were being broadcast out for others to hear?

No, definitely not. I've never felt like someone was putting thoughts in my head, and I don't feel like anyone can hear what I'm thinking. My thoughts are just... my own. Like I said, the only issue I'm having is when I try to explain things out loud to my team at work. Everything inside my head is completely normal and private.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
No, I haven't been feeling down or hopeless. I still enjoy the things I usually do. Like I said, it's just the talking part that's been a problem for me lately.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or had racing thoughts that wouldn't slow down?

No, I haven't. I sleep my regular amount... usually about seven or eight hours. I don't get, you know, bursts of energy or anything like that. My thoughts don't race. Like I was saying, it's really just the trouble getting my words out right when I'm trying to talk to the guys at the store. Everything else is pretty standard.
Has this problem with your speech ever happened outside of work, like when you're talking to friends or family members?

Yeah, it happens at home, too. It's gotten to the point where my wife has had to take over things I used to handle, like going to the bank or talking to the neighbors, because people were getting confused or... I don't know, uncomfortable around me. And at work, it's definitely affecting things. They don't trust me to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. My boss even pulled me aside after my last performance review and told me I might be suspended if I don't get it together. So, yeah, it's not just a small thing. It's happening everywhere.

Outside of the speech issues you've described, have you ever had difficulty organizing your behavior, like trouble completing tasks, staying focused, or acting in a way that others might find odd or inappropriate?

Well, yeah, I have noticed some things like that. Sometimes when I'm out on the sales floor, I'll catch myself just pacing the exact same aisle. I'll be straightening the same row of batteries over and over again. Or... I'll just be standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand, and the associates are all just waiting for me to tell them what to do, but I'm just standing there. So, yeah, it's been hard to stay focused on what I'm actually supposed to be getting done.
Have you ever had trouble organizing your thoughts or behavior, like not being able to complete tasks, acting in a way that others found strange, or doing things without a clear reason?

I think I just went over that a little bit. Like I was saying, I get stuck pacing the same aisle, fixing the same batteries, or just standing there with the schedule when I'm supposed to be directing the team. But other than what I just told you... no, I haven't noticed anything else. I don't think I do things without a reason, it's mostly just getting stuck and losing focus like I mentioned a second ago.
Do you ever notice your thoughts becoming disorganized or jumping around when you're not speaking out loud, like when you're trying to focus on a task or make a decision?

Not really, no. When I'm just thinking to myself, things seem pretty clear. They don't jump around or get jumbled up in my head. It's really just... when I'm actually trying to talk out loud to someone, or when I get stuck doing those repetitive things I mentioned. But as far as just sitting and thinking or making a decision in my own head, no, I haven't noticed any problem with that.
Have you ever had any beliefs that other people around you don’t share, like thinking that someone is following you, watching you, or that you have special abilities others don’t?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't think anyone is following me or watching me... nothing like that. And I definitely don't have any special abilities. I'm just, you know, a regular guy trying to get through my shifts at the store. So no, I haven't had any beliefs like what you're describing.
